cover: Has your team outgrown its spreadsheets?

slides.title: Does one status live in several places?
slides.body: At an auction house we built for, a sheet, a photo folder and a group chat each held part of an item's status. They drifted apart.

slides.title: Can anyone settle who changed it?
slides.body: The status changed in a sheet, a folder and a chat. No one history covered all three, so nothing could settle a disagreement.

slides.title: Could you get a deleted row back?
slides.body: Restoring an older file version also undoes everyone's later edits. A mistake the week before a sale meant rebuilding from memory.

slides.title: Do decisions stay in the chat?
slides.body: Decisions made in a chat thread never make it back into any record.

slides.title: Does only one person get the sheet?
slides.body: If only one person really understands it, that's a sign on its own.

slides.title: Then trace one recent disagreement
slides.body: Find where each version came from and decide who owns that information. You may fix part of it before replacing any software.
